blocks.text: MAT:100–122 DETAILED REVIEW STATUS — NOT CANONICAL

The nine-root first-principles review is complete. It compares the current Phase 2 meaning with three genuinely different replacements at every address, scores 36 candidates, supplies invariant definitions, boundaries, address analysis, tailored runtime states, six example types per root, eleven-family collision audits, and 82 English concept tests. Validation passed 23 checks and 2,592 deterministic generation assertions. No atom meaning or generated form changed.
Recommended semantic grid pending user decision:
MAT:100 — completed focal material change — Completion of a physical-state change localized within the focal material bearer.
MAT:101 — active focal material change — An ongoing physical-state change localized within the focal material bearer.
MAT:102 — potential focal material change — A possible physical-state change localized within the focal material bearer that is not active or completed.
MAT:110 — completed target material change — Completion of a physical-state change localized in a distinct material target.
MAT:111 — active target material change — An ongoing physical-state change localized in a distinct material target.
MAT:112 — potential target material change — A possible physical-state change localized in a distinct material target that is not active or completed.
MAT:120 — completed systemic material change — Completion of a physical-state change distributed across materially interacting parts of a shared system.
MAT:121 — active systemic material change — An ongoing physical-state change distributed across materially interacting parts of a shared system.
MAT:122 — potential systemic material change — A possible physical-state change distributed across materially interacting parts of a shared system that is not active or completed.

Design boundary: MAT:1xx owns intrinsic physical-state change. The second trit selects focal, target, or systemic locus; the third selects completed, ongoing, or possible-but-nonactualized phase. Position, transfer, structure, creation purpose, damage, restoration, living growth, information change, control flow, cause, magnitude, result, scheduling, queueing, readiness, probability, and future certainty are not silently absorbed. Transfer, force, resource, cycle, fabrication, and similar English concepts require other families, grammar, later MAT layers, or explicit compounds.

Current semantic authority remains 45 canonical roots and 279 provisional roots. MOV:200–222, MAT:000–022, and MAT:100–122 are reviewed but await user decisions: 27 reviewed-pending roots. The remaining semantic workload is 252 unreviewed roots in 28 nine-root chunks.

Translator consequence: the broad translator remains blocked. The safe prototype boundary is still an explicit-ID renderer over the 45 canonical roots that rejects provisional roots, unapproved compounds, and underspecified grammar.
Next semantic block after decisions on the three pending packets: MAT:200–222. No MAT:200–222 review, Gate 4 compound work, or translator implementation was begun in this packet.
